extracted.intended_audience: legal practitioners, DPA authors/auditors, and NLP/IR researchers building automated GDPR compliance-checking tools
extracted.subtask_description: Define and operationalize an NLP-based method (DERECHA) to check Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) against GDPR by (1) extracting a set of 45 compliance requirements, (2) representing requirements and DPA statements as semantic-frame (SF) predicate-argument structures, and (3) matching them to produce a compliance report.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (PO15) Information to demonstrate compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 (PO15) The processor shall make available to the controller information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations Article 28 in GDPR. (Art. 28(3)(h))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among the 45 extracted requirements. Treated as a processor's obligation (PO). Mandatory/optional status: R1–R26 are presented as mandatory in the paper (R21 included). Compliance checking requires finding a DPA statement whose SF-based representation matches this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: R22 (PO16) Allow and contribute to audits/inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: R22 (PO16) The processor shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or another auditor mandated by the controller. (Art. 28(3)(h))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processor obligation. Must be explicitly stated or captured semantically in the DPA. DERECHA looks for matching predicates/arguments (actor=processor, action=allow/contribute, object=audits/inspections, beneficiary=controller or controller-mandated auditor).

rubrics_metrics.name: R23 (PO17) Flow-down obligations to sub-processors
rubrics_metrics.description: R23 (PO17) The processor shall impose the same obligations on the engaged sub-processors by way of contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law. (Art. 28(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processor obligation requiring explicit contractual flow-down. Matching should capture the imposition of obligations on sub-processors and the contractual/legal-act mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: R24 (PO18) Processor remains fully liable for sub-processor performance
rubrics_metrics.description: R24 (PO18) The processor shall remain fully liable to the controller for the performance of sub-processor’s obligations. (Art. 28(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processor obligation specifying liability for sub-processor conduct. Compliance requires the DPA to reflect processor liability language or semantically equivalent phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: R25 (PO19) Security assessment must consider risks to personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: R25 (PO19) When assessing the level of security, the processor shall take into account the risk of accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alternation, unauthorized disclosure of or access to the personal data transmitted, stored or processed. (Art. 32(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processor obligation requiring explicit consideration of listed risks when implementing security measures. Matching should capture 'assess the level of security' and the enumerated risk types or close synonyms (enrichment helps).

rubrics_metrics.name: R26 (CR1) Controller's right to object to sub-processor changes
rubrics_metrics.description: R26 (CR1) In case of general written authorization, the controller shall have the right to object to changes concerning the addition or replacement of sub-processors, after having been informed of such intended changes by the processor. (Art. 8(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controller right. The DPA should include a provision that, where general authorization is given, the controller retains a right to object following notification. Matching must capture (1) general written authorization context, (2) notification, and (3) right to object to additions/replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: R7 (example) No engagement of sub-processor without prior authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: R7. The processor shall not engage a sub-processor without a prior specific or general written authorization of the controller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a running example in the paper (Table 4). Matching requires predicate/object/time/constraint (e.g., 'not engage' + 'sub-processor' + 'without prior specific or general written authorization of the controller'). Example demonstrates how missing constraint/time argument causes partial matching and lower matching degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata requirements (R1–R6, R27–R29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata requirements describe the content that a DPA has to cover, e.g., the duration of the agreement; R1 and R2 concern the identity and contact details of the data controller and processor; R3–R6 (from Art. 28(3)) include subject-matter and duration of the processing, the nature and purpose of the processing, the type of personal data and categories of data subjects, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements specify what items must appear in the DPA metadata (names, contact details, duration, subject-matter, processing nature/purpose, data types/categories). DERECHA handles R1/R2 by looking for provided names and contact-details via regexes; R3–R6 and R27–R29 are verified via an overlap-based Lesk-inspired method (word overlap between requirement text and DPA statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of requirements: MD, PO, CR, CO
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance requirements are grouped into four categories: metadata requirements (MD), processor’s obligations (PO), controller’s rights (CR), and controller’s obligations (CO). The paper extracted 45 requirements and grouped them accordingly (nine MD, 25 PO, three CR, eight CO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The category affects representation decisions: SF-based representations are defined for PO, CR, and CO (R7–R25, R30–R45), while metadata requirements are handled with special methods (see Step E). Most mandatory requirements describe processor obligations (19/25).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory vs Optional classification
rubrics_metrics.description: From GDPR and expert feedback the authors identify 26 mandatory and 19 optional requirements among the 45 extracted; mandatory requirements (R1–R26) are explicitly stipulated in GDPR except R1 and R2 which were strongly recommended by legal experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DERECHA issues a non-compliance decision when a mandatory requirement is violated and raises a warning when an optional requirement is violated. This classification is used in the final compliance decision/report.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-based representation (predicate-arguments) for requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each compliance requirement is transformed into an SF (semantic frame) represented as a predicate and a set of arguments. The predicate highlights the main action; arguments correspond to SRs (semantic roles) such as actor, object, reason, time, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One SF is defined per requirement even if predicates repeat across requirements. SF representations are manually created once (step A) and reused across DPAs. Example: PO6 (R12) predicate 〈take〉 with arguments {actor=[the processor], object=[all measures], reference=[Article 32], reason=[to ensure the security of processing]}.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Semantic Roles (SRs) for DPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A collated list of 10 SRs pertinent to DPA compliance: action, actor, object, beneficiary, reason, time, condition, situation, reference, constraint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These SRs are used both to define SFs for GDPR requirements and to generate SFs for each DPA statement. Examples and expected realization patterns are provided (e.g., actor is NP subject of root verb; action is VP containing root verb).

rubrics_metrics.name: SR extraction rules (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to extract SRs from a statement: action = VP containing root verb; actor = NP containing subject of root verb; object = NP containing object of root verb or VP starting with a preposition associated with root verb; beneficiary, condition, constraint, time, reason, situation, reference defined via dependency patterns and markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These extraction rules rely mainly on dependency parsing and chunking. Statements without a root verb (e.g., titles) are not represented. The rules are adaptations from relation-extraction literature and include examples from the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markers for identifying SRs (Table 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example SR markers used to detect roles: Beneficiary markers: inform, report, assist, help, notify, provide, etc.; Condition markers: if, once, in case, where, when; Constraint markers: without, on, in accordance with, according to, by, under, unless; Time markers: after, later, prior, before, as long as; Situation markers: access, addition, destruction, loss, disclosure, termination; Reference markers: gdpr, dpa, law, article, contract, jurisprudence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markers were augmented with synonyms from WordNet/VerbNet and tailored to GDPR expectations to improve recall on diverse DPA wordings. Markers drive SR identification rules in step C1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing NLP pipeline modules
rubrics_metrics.description: The preprocessing pipeline includes seven modules: (1) tokenization, (2) sentence splitting, (3) lemmatization, (4) POS tagging, (5) chunking, (6) dependency parsing, (7) semantic parsing (WordNet & VerbNet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each module produces annotations used downstream for SR identification, text span demarcation, enrichment, and SF generation. The implementation uses OpenNLP, Mate lemmatizer, Stanford dependency parser, WordNet/VerbNet access libraries as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text enrichment guidelines (Step D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enrich DPA text spans by extending them with semantically-related words: synonyms from WordNet for words in spans; verbs from the same VerbNet class for action spans. Replace actual controller/processor names with placeholders 'the controller' and 'the processor'. Use the most frequent sense (MFS) when selecting synonyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrichment increases chance of overlap when matching requirements; MFS is used as a pragmatic WSD baseline. Named-entity normalization helps matching across documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate matching conditions (E.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two predicates (requirement vs statement) match if (Condition 1) they have overlapping verbs, or (Condition 2) the Wu & Palmer (WuP) semantic similarity between the verb in the requirement and at least one verb in the statement ≥ θp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic similarity metric used: WuP (WordNet-based), producing scores in [0.0,1.0]. Empirically set predicate threshold θp = 0.9 to limit comparisons and ensure high similarity; only statements with similar predicates are considered for argument matching (efficiency and precision reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument matching procedure (E.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Align each required argument (SR) in the requirement to an argument in the DPA statement that shares the same SR label; enrich statement spans and then check for overlap or similarity between text spans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarity for arguments uses Jaro-Winkler distance; an argument pair is matching if text spans overlap or similarity ≥ θa. θa is empirically set to 0.7. Arguments present in the statement but not required are ignored; arguments required by GDPR but absent are marked as missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching degree computation (E.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a statement that passes predicate matching, compute matching degree = (found + 1) / (len(Ar) + 1), where found = number of matched arguments and Ar = set of required arguments for the requirement. The +1 accounts for the predicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requirement's score is the maximum matching degree across all statements in the DPA. Statements that match only the predicate but none of the arguments still receive a small (>0) score. Matching degree serves as a confidence indicator to guide analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final compliance decision rule (E.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A requirement is marked satisfied if at least one DPA statement satisfies the requirement (score ≠ 0); otherwise it is marked violated. A DPA is considered not compliant when at least one mandatory requirement is violated; optional requirement violations raise warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report lists violations and warnings. The tool recommends analysts review low-confidence matches (low matching degrees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Lesk-inspired overlap for metadata requirements (E: Metadata verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: For metadata requirements R3–R6 and R27–R29 the method is inspired by Lesk: find a statement in the DPA that has overlapping words with the requirement (word overlap between requirement text and DPA statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically motivated because manual analysis showed common wordings for metadata items. Implemented as a simpler overlap check rather than full SF matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation/tooling choices as operational guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation details: Java implementation; Apache POI to extract text from MS Word; DKPro toolkit (OpenNLP tokenizer/POS/chunker, Mate lemmatizer, Stanford dependency parser); extJWNL for WordNet; JVerbNet for VerbNet; WS4J for WuP and Jaro-Winkler metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These choices illustrate a reproducible pipeline; alternatives could be used but must provide the same types of annotations (chunks, dependencies, lemma, WordNet/VerbNet access, similarity metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design decision: one predicate per statement
rubrics_metrics.description: DERECHA generates one predicate for each DPA statement (sentence) — the main action (root verb) — rather than multiple predicates per sentence as in typical SRL tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: GDPR requirement SFs are centered around one predicate; extracting one predicate reduces noise and computational cost. Statements without a root verb are not represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of enrichment and marker-synonym expansion to increase recall
rubrics_metrics.description: Markers for SRs are enriched with synonyms from WordNet and VerbNet, and SR-specific nouns/verbs observed in GDPR SFs are added to cover different wordings in DPAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pragmatic augmentation increases the likelihood of matching diverse phrasing across DPAs and GDPR requirements, at the cost of needing good lexical resources and careful marker selection.
